text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.74% today to $126.59, continuing a sharp two-week decline of 6.26%. The main driver is a sustained drop in oil prices: U.S. crude has tumbled from the $140s range earlier this month to $107 per barrel today, largely on hopes that diplomatic talks between the U.S. and Iran could ease Middle East tensions and restore oil supply to global markets. When oil prices fall, exploration and production companies like ConocoPhillips see their revenues and profits squeezed, which is why the stock has tracked the oil selloff lower day after day.

The uncertainty itself is also weighing on the sector. Multiple reports on Monday and Tuesday mentioned that Wall Street analysts openly admit they don't know where oil is headed amid shifting diplomatic signals—Trump signaling openness to talks, then Iran offering to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week. That kind of whipsaw in expectations (from war risk pushing oil up to peace hopes pushing it down) tends to keep energy stocks under pressure until the situation becomes clearer.
